summary: Defines a DHCP option that a client can use to say what kind of user or application it represents. The information is an opaque value, and the server can use it to choose which pool of addresses or settings to hand out. It is on the standards track.

eli5.summary: When you join a club, you can say which group you belong to, and the helper hands you the right kind of badge. This lets a computer say which group it is in when asking for an address.

questions: what is the dhcp user class option
how to give different addresses to different dhcp clients
how to give different dhcp settings to different clients
subtitle: A DHCP option that lets a client say what kind of user or software it represents, so the server can pick the right settings.

tldr.problem: DHCP servers normally cannot tell what category of user or application a client represents, so they cannot easily hand out different pools or settings to different groups.
tldr.mechanism: The User Class option (code 77) carries one or more opaque, length-prefixed class values chosen by the user or administrator, and the server uses them to choose an address pool and other configuration.
tldr.outcome: Servers ignore classes they do not understand. DHCP has no authentication, so a server cannot check that a client is allowed to claim a class.

today: RFC 3004 is a Proposed Standard, and the unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Purpose of the User Class Option
sections.content:
DHCP administrators may define their own user class identifiers to convey information about a client's software configuration or about its user's preferences. The RFC's example is configuring clients of people in the accounting department with a different printer than clients of people in the marketing department.

A DHCP client uses the User Class option to identify the type or category of user or applications it represents. The class is an opaque field. The server uses it to choose the address pool it allocates from and, or, to select any other configuration option. The option should be configurable by a user.
sections.eli5: A computer can say which group it belongs to, like accounting or marketing. The helper then gives it the right printer.

sections.title: Terminology
sections.content:
The RFC uses the requirement words (MUST, SHOULD, MAY and so on) as defined in RFC 2119. It also defines three DHCP terms.

  • A DHCP client is an Internet host using DHCP to obtain configuration parameters such as a network address.
  • A DHCP server is an Internet host that returns configuration parameters to clients.
  • A binding is a collection of configuration parameters, including at least an IP address, bound to a client and managed by servers.
sections.eli5: A client asks, a server answers, and a binding is the set of things the server gives that client.

sections.title: The Option Format
sections.content:
The User Class option is a normal DHCP option (see RFC 2131 and RFC 2132). Its code is 77, followed by a length Len and then the value, which holds one or more instances of User Class Data.

Each instance is a one-octet length UC_Len_i followed by that many octets of opaque data. The length does not count itself and MUST be non-zero.

The option's Len must equal the sum of all the class lengths plus m, the number of classes: Len = UC_Len_1 + UC_Len_2 + ... + UC_Len_m + m. When at least one class is present, the smallest possible Len is 2.
sections.eli5: Each class name is written with its length in front, like a label that says how long the word is. Several labels can be put in a row.

sections.title: How Clients and Servers Use It
sections.content:
The option MAY carry multiple user classes. Servers may interpret multiple classes in an implementation or configuration dependent way, so a client should choose its classes based on the specific server setup that will process them.

A server that cannot interpret a given class MUST ignore it, though it may report it. If a server recognizes some of the classes a client sent but not others, it MAY use the ones it recognizes.

Clients that implement the option SHOULD let users enter one or more user class values.
sections.eli5: If the helper does not know a group name, it skips it. If it knows some names, it can use those.

sections.title: IANA Considerations
sections.content: Option 77, which IANA had already assigned for this purpose, is the one to use as the User Class option for DHCP. The RFC asks for no new assignments.
sections.eli5: The number 77 was already reserved for this job, so nothing new has to be set aside.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
DHCP currently provides no authentication or security mechanisms, and the exposures to attack are discussed in section 7 of RFC 2131.

As a result, a DHCP server cannot check whether a client or user is authorized to use a given user class. That is an obvious weakness when the class is used to hand out something special, such as a particular database server: there is no way to authenticate the client or confirm it may use that parameter.
sections.eli5: Anyone can say they are on the team, and the helper cannot check. So do not hand out secrets just because someone named a group.
